remaining: Ethniki Insurance IT integration; DORA/ICT incident metrics; Ukraine/Germany fleet; final md write

signals.signal: CMD 2026-30 deck (05/03/2026) quantifies the AI programme for the first time: CapEx 2026-2030 ~EUR 800mn of which ~80% for AI/technology, plus ~EUR 50mn CapEx for Ethniki Insurance transformation ('five year CapEx of EUR 850mn'); AI-driven capacity release is booked as ~EUR 50mn staff-cost and ~EUR 20mn G&A efficiencies (~EUR 60mn inside the plan); OpEx walk 2025 EUR 0.9bn to ~EUR 1.0bn 2030 carries explicit -EUR 40mn AI (staff) and -EUR 20mn AI (G&A) lines against +EUR 25mn technology and +EUR 15mn IT; EUR 8-10mn efficiencies from Attica HQ reorganisation.
signals.source_name: Piraeus Group - Strategic Plan 2026-2030 Capital Markets Day presentation (PDF, slides 'Enhanced productivity' / 'OpEX walk 2025-2030')
signals.implies: An ~EUR 640mn AI/technology budget with a board-committed EUR 60-70mn cost-out target. Printec should sell managed services and self-service automation as the delivery vehicle for the capacity-release number, not as capex.
signals.likelihood: Spending already running (IT capex c.EUR 140mn p.a. 2024-26); procurement continuous through the plan
signals.followup: Pull the Strategic Plan IRToolkit XLSX and the CMD Q&A transcript to see any software/equipment split; ask IR what share of the ~80% AI/tech is third-party vendor spend vs Newra/Accenture.

signals.signal: Assured Sustainability Statement 2025 gives audited fleet metrics that differ materially from the c.1,500 marketing figure: ATMs of Piraeus Group in Greece 1,641 at 31/12/2025 (2,092 at 31/12/2024, i.e. -451 after the Cashflex/KEA carve-out); of the 1,641, 1,197 offer deposit with immediate cash availability (1,201 in 2024); 1,172 ATMs had voice-guidance software installed and operating at end-2025 (1,097 in 2024, +75); ATMs outside Greece 19 (18 in Ukraine, rest Germany); branches in Greece 368 (368 in 2024), outside Greece 16 (15 Ukraine + Frankfurt).
signals.source_name: Piraeus Group Sustainability Statement 2025 (Table 80 'ATMs & Branches' and section 'ATMs'), pp.92-93
signals.implies: The real addressable Greek fleet is 1,641, not 1,500 - c.140 more units than the investor deck implies. 444 units are still withdrawal-only and are the recycler upgrade white space; 469 units still lack voice guidance, a compliance-driven software/retrofit opportunity of the same shape Printec already delivers at Alpha and in Romania.
signals.likelihood: Voice-guidance retrofit is running at c.75 units/yr and will continue; deposit-capable share flat, so a recycler refresh decision is due
signals.followup: Reconcile 1,641 (audited) vs c.1,500 (CMD/H1 decks) vs the c.934 in-branch + c.360 remote split carried in the baseline - ask IR which perimeter each uses; confirm whether the 444 non-deposit units are the island/remote estate.

signals.signal: First published forward branch-reduction commitment: 'Piraeus Bank intends to safeguard unimpeded access... by maintaining its level of available branches above 300 units in the next four (4) years. More specifically, albeit with increased offering of digital channels, physical networks are planned to be reduced by 2% Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) for the 4-year period.' This contradicts the 'flat estate' reading of the quarterly decks (368 domestic branches unchanged 2024, 2025 and Jun-2026).
signals.source_name: Piraeus Group Sustainability Statement 2025, section following Table 80 (ATMs & Branches)
signals.implies: -2% CAGR takes 368 branches to roughly 340 by 2029 while transactions migrate to self-service. Consolidation of branches is the classic trigger for recycler density increases, off-site ATM redeployment and VTS/kiosk substitution - all Printec lines.
signals.likelihood: Stated four-year plan; first closures should show in the quarterly branch count during 2026-27
signals.followup: Track domestic branch count each quarter for the first decline; ask whether closed-branch ATMs are retained as off-site units or sold into the Cashflex network.

signals.signal: Sustainability Statement 2025 names Video Teller Systems (VTS) and Digital Kiosks as accessibility infrastructure 'being scaled through 2025 and beyond', alongside Braille cards, voice-guided ATMs and sign-language-trained staff. Separately, CapEx on new IT solutions related to customer services was EUR 50.4mn in 2025 (EUR 50.5mn in 2024) across 270 selected projects, and Piraeus' IT CapEx is 75% of total technology spend versus a 22% average across the c.300 financial institutions in the Gartner benchmark.
signals.source_name: Piraeus Group Sustainability Statement 2025 ('Equal and Unobstructed Access for all'; Table 78a 'Innovation and Efficiency')
signals.implies: An explicit, funded VTS + digital kiosk rollout - the exact remote-teller/assisted-service hardware and software Printec supplies (and that CrediaBank is buying via CrediaConnect/FORTH). A 75%-capex IT mix vs 22% peer average means Piraeus buys assets, not subscriptions, which favours hardware-plus-managed-service bids.
signals.likelihood: Rollout stated as ongoing; no unit counts published
signals.followup: Find the VTS/kiosk unit counts and the incumbent vendor - not disclosed anywhere yet; check whether the in-branch information kiosks flagged in the H1-2026 deck are the same devices.

signals.signal: CMD deck names Agentic AI pilots by function, including Compliance ('triage review and assessment') and Risk ('monitoring, early warning'), plus Network first-point-of-contact, CIB, wealth advisory, central-function transactional processes and marketing; portfolio of 50 GenAI use cases of which 13 revenue-generating; >75% target adoption of AI tools; 15% of existing capacity to be unlocked through technology and AI; efficiencies from AI and technology ~EUR 70mn (~80% booked in the plan).
signals.source_name: Piraeus Group - Strategic Plan 2026-2030 CMD presentation ('AI-driven growth'; 'Agentic AI innovation in progress')
signals.implies: Piraeus intends to build compliance triage and risk monitoring in-house on agentic AI with Accenture/Newra. Headwind for Printec's AML/compliance and transaction-monitoring line; the openable door is data plumbing and the Bank of Greece 2026 on-site inspection priority on transaction-monitoring systems.
signals.followup: Establish whether the compliance triage layer sits on top of a third-party monitoring engine or replaces one, and which engine.

signals.signal: Piraeus Bank S.A. is one of 36 payment service providers selected by the Eurosystem on 14/07/2026 for the digital euro pilot - one of only three Greek entrants (with National Bank of Greece and the Cooperative Bank of Chania). The pilot runs at the ECB and 19 national central banks, starts in H2 2027 and lasts 12 months, testing a beta digital euro in real-life in-shop and person-to-person payments; the list of locations where PSPs will offer pilot services is to be finalised later in 2026.
signals.source_name: European Central Bank - 'ECB selects 36 payment service providers to join digital euro pilot' + digital euro pilot page (participant list)
signals.implies: Digital euro acceptance means POS/terminal software changes, card and wallet issuance, and an eventual ATM funding/defunding use case (cash-to-digital-euro at the ATM). Printec's POS/acquiring and ATM application lines are both in scope for pilot-driven integration work in 2026-27.
signals.likelihood: Preparation work with the Bank of Greece starts now; pilot H2 2027
signals.followup: Watch for the location list later in 2026 and ask Piraeus which channels (app, card, POS, ATM) it will pilot; check whether the Bank of Greece publishes a Greek workstream.

signals.signal: Piraeus is the first Greek bank certified to ISO/IEC 42001:2023 (AI management systems). Certificate issued by TUV NORD Hellas S.A., three-year validity, effective 01/04/2026, announced 07/07/2026. Scope covers the bank's overall AI governance framework plus two named applications: the customer-facing Digital Assistant (e-banking and mobile app) and the internal Employee Assistant on the Yello platform, with emphasis on risk management, transparency, accountability and continuous monitoring; framed as EU AI Act readiness.
signals.source_name: Oikonomikos Tachydromos (ot.gr) - 'Peiraios: i proti elliniki trapeza me pistopoiisi ISO/IEC 42001 gia tin AI'
signals.implies: A certified AIMS raises the bar for any vendor selling AI-touching software into Piraeus: AML/monitoring, eKYC liveness and fraud scoring will now be audited against the bank's 42001 controls. Printec should be able to evidence AI governance artefacts in bids.
signals.likelihood: Certificate live since 01/04/2026; surveillance audits annually
signals.followup: Find the Piraeus press-office original (press-office/news-announcements) for the certificate scope statement; the ot.gr piece is press-tier only.

signals.signal: CMD deck: Snappi operationally launched October 2025, 'low-capex expansion model with no branches', target 300k clients in the next 12 months (from ~210k app users at H1-2026); products are account, debit card, payments, savings at 1% interest, Pay Later and 'Cash Now' instant interest-free loan up to EUR 1,000; strategy framed as 'attack neobanks (Snappi), defend young and tech-savvy portion of own clientele (Piraeus app)'. Separately, on 30/03/2026 Snappi appointed Paymentology as issuer-processor for its scaling phase, covering card and payment functions, real-time processing and regulatory readiness.
signals.source_name: Piraeus CMD presentation 05/03/2026 ('Snappi: the Group's neobank'); Paymentology newsroom, 'Paymentology Supports the Next Phase of Growth for Snappi'
signals.implies: Card processing at Snappi is now foreclosed to Paymentology and the core is Natech. What is left for Printec is digital onboarding/eKYC and AML screening capacity behind a 300k-client ramp - and nothing in cash or self-service, by design.
signals.likelihood: Client target is management ambition; Paymentology contract signed
signals.followup: Identify Snappi's KYC/AML vendor and whether onboarding is Natech-native or third-party.

signals.signal: Re-verified on primary sources this run. The audited FY2025 Board report confirms the 22/05/2025 sale of 80.1% of KEA Leitourgia kai Diacheirisi Diktyon ATM S.M.S.A. to Printec Cash Network S.A., loss of control, and the 19.9% residual now equity-accounted; it states the Bank still operates 'the second largest ATM network in the country with 1,500 units (both in branches and off-site)'. Cashflex's own site (re-fetched with a desktop User-Agent after a fetch-tool block) still advertises only 'quick cash withdrawals, balance inquiries, and PIN changes' - no deposit anywhere on the network - describes 'hundreds' of ATMs without publishing a count, and is still actively recruiting partner sites. The Cashflex newsroom has published nothing since 01/10/2025.
signals.source_name: Piraeus Bank S.A. Annual Financial Report 31 December 2025, BoD Report ('Sale of Kea Leitourgia kai Diacheirisi Diktyon ATM'); cashflex.gr About / Partners / News pages
signals.implies: The whole c.850-unit off-site estate remains withdrawal-only. Every unit is a candidate for a deposit/recycling upgrade, and the ATM fee cap (zero own-network, EUR 1.50 third-party since 11/08/2025) makes deposit-capability the only remaining way to add revenue per site. This is Printec's own asset, so the sale is internal - but it is the single largest recycler-conversion pool in Greece.
signals.likelihood: No published upgrade plan; decision is Printec's own
signals.followup: Get a current unit count from Cashflex directly (the site refuses to publish one; press figures are 850 at carve-out and '220 live, 800 by autumn' from Jul-2025) and test the business case for deposit-enabling the estate under the fee cap.
